units.text: INT. HOTEL BALLROOM - ARBITRATION - DAY
A rented ballroom.
Chandeliers, stacking chairs, a banquet table draped in white.
Through the folding partition, wedding music thumps: a bass line, a cheering crowd.
ARBITRATOR HENRIETTA BOSCO, 60s, sits at the head of the table with a legal pad and a stopwatch.
She wears reading glasses on a chain and an expression of hard-won patience.
To her left: CLAIMANT DARNELL FITZGIBBON, 40s, in a suit that doesn't quite close, and his attorney, LUCINDA TAN-ROSSI, 30s, with a color-coded binder.
To her right: RESPONDENT GUSTAV HALVERSEN, 60s, silver beard, folded hands, and his attorney, AMBROSE KELLEHER, 50s, with a fountain pen he clicks constantly.
A paralegal, BRIGITTE, 20s, sits at the end with a laptop and a timer.
The wedding bass drops.
Everyone flinches.
Mr. Keller... Kelleher. Your opening.
units.name: BOSCO

units.text: Thank you, Arbitrator. My client, Mr. Halversen, has operated this ballroom for twenty years.
units.name: KELLEHER

units.text: And has never once fixed the ceiling.
units.name: LUCINDA

units.text: I was not finished.
units.name: KELLEHER

units.text: Ms. Tan-Rossi, wait your turn.
units.name: BOSCO

units.text: Apologies, Arbitrator. I was moved.
units.name: LUCINDA

units.text: She grins.
Darnell elbows her.
Halversen studies the chandelier above them.
A crystal quivers with the bass.
The roof has been inspected annually.
units.name: KELLEHER

units.text: It fell on my cousin's wedding cake.
units.name: DARNELL

units.text: It was a small piece of ceiling.
units.name: HALVERSEN

units.text: It was the size of a hubcap!
units.name: DARNELL

units.text: Mr. Fitzgibbon, you will address counsel, not the respondent.
units.name: BOSCO

units.text: Sorry, Arbitrator.
units.name: DARNELL

units.text: She lowers her glasses.
He sinks into his seat.
Brigitte whispers to Lucinda, who nods, flips three tabs, and slides a photograph across the table.
Exhibit Nine. The cake, post-impact.
units.name: LUCINDA

units.text: Bosco picks up the photograph.
She studies it for a long moment.
Something almost like a smile crosses her face and is quickly put away.
Mr. Halversen, did you replace the cake?
units.name: BOSCO

units.text: Madame, I replaced the ceiling.
units.name: HALVERSEN

units.text: That wasn't my question.
units.name: BOSCO

units.text: Halversen unfolds his hands.
Refolds them.
Kelleher stops clicking his pen.
A cheer rises from the wedding.
A woman's voice over a microphone: "And now, the first dance!"
Everyone at the table turns toward the partition.
The music slows to something soft.
We will take ten minutes.
units.name: BOSCO

units.text: She stands.
The others stand.
Darnell, Halversen, the lawyers, all of them drift toward the divider, and no one says why.
